def _parallel_fit_estimator(estimator, X, y, sample_weight=None):
    """Private function used to fit an estimator within a job."""
    if sample_weight is not None:
        estimator.fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)
    else:
        estimator.fit(X, y)
    return estimator

Deliver patch-2 (workspace v3): sklearn/ensemble/voting.py fix + regression test.

Behavior fix: _BaseVoting.fit (parent of VotingClassifier and VotingRegressor) validated sample_weight support over every entry of self.estimators, including entries set to None by set_params(name=None). has_fit_parameter reached step.fit and raised AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fit' — exactly the issue's traceback for voter.fit(X, y, sample_weight=...) after voter.set_params(lr=None). The check now skips disabled (None) estimators, so the issue's snippet fits successfully.

Edge cases preserved: estimators that genuinely lack sample_weight support still raise ValueError('Underlying estimator <name> does not support sample weights.') — the new test asserts this for KNeighborsClassifier after also disabling lr. Downstream fit/predict logic is untouched; VotingRegressor shares this code path so it is fixed too.

Evidence on this exact version (v3): sklearn/ensemble/tests/test_voting.py — 19 collected, 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. This includes the newly added test_sample_weight_after_estimator_set_to_none, which exercises the issue's exact sequence rather than only the pre-existing sample_weight tests (which the earlier delivery relied on and which do not cover the None-estimator path).
